tossups.text: The strength of one component of this phenomenon is measured as the difference in surface pressure between Tahiti and Darwin. Although not global warming, this phenomenon increases vertical wind shear, which adversely impacts the strength of hurricanes. That component is the Walker circulation. One of the strongest occurrences of this phenomenon, in 1983, marked the start of mass coral bleaching. This phenomenon causes a warm current to appear off the coast of Peru, preventing upwelling due to the cold Humboldt current. For 10 points, name this irregular cycle of warming and cooling in the eastern Pacific.

A coalition supporting this good criticized a certain act as the "Crime of '73" and supported a specific 16-to-1 ratio. The Bland-Allison Act forced the Treasury to recurrently buy this good. One speech which advocated introducing this good to a certain system claims "You shall not press down upon the brow of labor this crown of thorns". Miners rushed to Nevada after this metal was discovered at the Comstock Lode. Populists advocated for fixing currency to this good in a bimetallic system. For 10 points, a "Free" movement named after what precious metal opposed the gold standard?

This animal appears in the title of a novel in which a chauffeur writes letters to Wen Jiabao about how he murdered his employer. This animal also appears in the interrogative title of a short story in which a king uses a method of justice that ends in either a brutal slaughter or a wedding. Rudyard Kipling created one of these animals named Shere Khan, and in the Yann Martel novel Life of Pi, the character Richard Parker is one of these animals. For 10 points, name this animal that titles a poem in which it is "Burning bright / In the forests of the night."

This resource can be obtained through structures whose "artesian" type are powered by natural pressure without the need for pumping. Overdrafting for agriculture is causing the depletion of a major source of this resource in the American Great Plains called the Ogallala Aquifer. In many rural areas, this resource is stored in "towers". For 10 points, what resource might be extracted from the ground via a well?

His chief agents were Alvise Cadamosto and Diogo Gomes. He was a distinguished fighter in the capture of Ceuta from the Moors and sponsored another successful campaign in Morocco in 1458. However, he spent more attention sending agents to the Madeira Islands, Cape Bojador, and Cape Blanco. His men colonized the Azores and began to push deeper into Africa, establishing a base at his school at Sagres. For 10 points, name this son of King Joao I, Portuguese royal known for his patronage of explorers.

The change in this quantity from a canonical transform is the time derivative of the generating function and this quantity is the negative partial time derivative of action. Partial derivatives of this quantity yield the canonical equations. The Poisson bracket with this quantity generates a time derivative, which proves this quantity is conserved for time invariant systems. To find this quantity for a system one frequently needs to Legendre transform the Lagrangian. For 10 points, what is this quantity, the basis of a namesake mechanics that, like a quantum mechanical operator of the same name, represents the total energy of a system?

This conceptual group was supported by Athanasius's description of homoousios, or a "single essence,"and was opposed by Arianism, which said that Jesus had instead been created by God. Belief in this group is declared in the Nicene Creed, which says that there is a shared holiness between the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. For 10 points, name this group of three aspects of the Christian God.

The protagonist of this novel claims "I say to myself... you are a tree." After discovering that two lost children are alive on a missionary trip to Africa, a character in this novel discovers her real father was a store owner who was lynched. In this novel, retaliating against a slap from the mayor's wife Miss Millie gets Sofia arrested. The protagonist of this novel is married to a man referred to only as "Mister" before falling in love with Shug Avery. For 10 points, name this novel in which Celia writes letters to God, by Alice Walker.

In this novel, Major Imbu discusses the murder of Stilson while Bonzo's body is being transported back to Spain. Two siblings in this novel adopt the screen names Demosthenes and Locke to gain political influence, and one of them becomes the Hegemon of Earth. At the end of this novel, the title character meets Mazer Rackham and wins the Bug War. For 10 points, name this novel about a young title military genius, written by Orson Scott Card.

To dissolve this group of elements, rings consisting of multiple ether groups can trap them in their cores. Saponification usually uses ions of these elements to make soaps consisting of their fatty acid salts. Pure samples of these elements are stored in kerosene or mineral oil. These elements exhibit a dramatic increase from their first ionization energy to their second ionization energy. Pure samples of these elements react explosively in water. Since these elements have the largest radii and smallest ionization energies in their period, they form ions with plus-one charge. For 10 points, potassium and lithium are part of what group of metals, the leftmost on the periodic table?

In one story, this man interpreted falling off his horse as a bad omen, causing him to not join his son on an exploration out west. This man had a dispute with his neighbor after he lent him his seat posts, but his neighbor refused to return them. His subsequent killing of that neighbor brought about his exile for three years. During that exile, he established an estate at Brattahlith. This man's son discovered Vinland, which is located on the east coast of North America. For 10 points, name this father of Leif Ericson and Viking explorer who created the first settlements in Greenland.

Examples of these people include the kauwa in Hawaii. In 1962, about 300,000 of these people benefitted from the Ten-Point Program put forth by Faisal in Saudi Arabia. These people were helped by the Somerset case in England, and examples in Greece included the penestae of Thessaly. In South America, descendants of these people were the subject of a law named for a kind of "womb." These people were helped by the passage of the Golden Law under Isabella, regent for Pedro II in Brazil. In England, a prominent critic of the treatment of these people was William Wilberforce. Article 4 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights outlaws the creation of these people. For 10 points, name these people, the subject of the Thirteenth Amendment, which emancipated them.

The board governing this policy was first chaired by former New Hampshire governor John G. Winant. This policy caused Senator Thomas Gore to ask, "Isn't this a teeny-weeny bit of socialism?" The Supreme Court case Flemming v. Nestor established that Congress can revise and amend this policy, which was expanded to include disability in 1954. This program includes the spousal survivor benefit and is funded through FICA taxes. For 10 points, name this largest American entitlement program, which gives monthly payouts to people who are 65 and older.

The SPT technique, which uses selective applications of a pi pulse, was a fore-runner of one form of it, and another form makes the use of Magic Angle Spinning to eliminate line broadening. Its two dimensional form which provides information about bond connectivity is called COSY. The Pascal's triangle can be used to model the splitting of peaks when the spins of neighboring particles are coupled, and it uses tetra-methyl-silane as its base to measure the relative chemical shift of the sample. For 10 points, identify this form of spectroscopy wherein a magnetic field is applied to a sample, which is frequently performed in its Carbon 13 and Proton varieties.

The protagonist in one of his novels accuses his brother of being illegitimate after that brother receives an inheritance from Leon Marechal. This author also wrote a story in which the protagonist is stabbed with a cheese knife by Rachel. This author of Pierre et Jean and " Mademoiselle Fifi" wrote about a character that is persuaded to sleep with a Prussian officer. In another of his stories, the protagonist attempts to repay a possession of Madame Forestier only to find that it is worth only 500 francs. For 10 points, name this author of "Ball of Fat" who wrote about Madame Loisel in "The Necklace."

A character in one play by this author threatens to disrupt the coronation of Queen Victoria if the sheriff cannot prevent an elopement. The protagonist of a play by this author sings "The Song of Great Capitulation," which convinces a soldier to withdraw his complaints. This playwright described acting in a way that prevented the audience from identifying with the characters in the play to achieve a "distancing effect." He's not John Gay, but "Mack the Knife" marries Polly Peachum in a play by this author. Anna Fierling travels in a wagon to sell supplies to soldiers in the Thirty Years' War with her children Kattrin, Eilif, and Swiss Cheese in another of this author's plays. For 10 points, name this playwright of The Threepenny Opera and Mother Courage and Her Children.

this structure is essential for white blood cell types. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in white blood cell types.

tossups.text: Description acceptable. The account of one of these events by John of Ephesus describes headless black people rowing phantom bronze ships through the air. The death of Emperor Claudius Gothicus in one of these events encouraged mass conversions to Christianity according to St. Cyprian of Carthage. An account of one of these events claims that a leader was too upset by the death of Paralus and Xanthippus during it to be consoled by Aspasia. The return of Lucius Verus's troops began one of these events during the reign of Marcus Aurelius known as the "Antonine" one. The Secret History of Procopius blames a devastating event of this type on the evil of Emperor Justinian, and one of them killed Pericles during a siege by Sparta. For 10 points, the population of Athens in 430 BCE was decimated by what type of disaster?

The speaker of one of this author's poems receives the title objects, which were "knitted with threads of twilight and goatskin," from Mari Mori. This author included that "Ode to My Socks" with odes to clam chowder and tuna in his Elemental Odes. In a poetry collection translated by W. S. Merwin, this author wrote "tonight I can write the saddest lines." This poet wrote "arise to birth with me, my brother," in a Canto from his "The Heights of Macchu Picchu." For 10 points, name this Chilean poet who penned Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair.

Rett syndrome has been associated with hypermodification of certain classes of these proteins. During spermatogenesis, they are replaced by the arginine-rich protamines, which are necessary for sperm head condensation. The largest of these, class 1, links octameric units of the other four classes. These proteins are rich in positively charged amino acids such as lysine, which is often modified in them by acetyl groups. Four types of these form part of a unit spanning 146 base pairs called a nucleosome, which is key for the supercoiling of DNA. For 10 points, name these proteins around which DNA wraps to form chromatin.

parts.text: Name these expenditures incurred by participating in a market.

"The Nature of the Firm" was an early paper by this economist. He showed that if transaction costs were assumed to be zero and property rights were well-defined, externalities could be internalized regardless of the initial allocation of property rights in "The Problem of Social Cost."

Another economist that has argued for the importance of clearly defined property rights is this Peruvian. This founder of the Institute for Liberty and Democracy described the extralegal system of property rights created by squatters in the outskirts of Lima in his book The Other Path.

bonuses.leadin: The paper "The Nature of the Firm" argues that these expenditures explain why companies hire employees rather than contract out all work. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Named for the Black Sea port in which it was held, this conference was the last among Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin. It saw the Allies agree to the 4 postwar occupation zones in Germany, among other things.

The Potsdam Conference, occurring during the final week of World War II, saw this man, head of the Labour Party, replace Churchill as the British Prime Minister and chief delegate. He was succeeded by Churchill in 1951.

This agreement, named for the city in which it was agreed, saw Cordell Hull, Anthony Eden, and Vyacheslav Molotov announce Allied intent towards war criminals. The status of Austria and Italy was also announced.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about Allied conferences and agreements during World War II.

parts.text: Name this novel that details Rupa Mehra's attempts to find a husband for her daughter Lata.
A Suitable Boy was written by this author of An Equal Music. This author used Pushkin sonnets for his novel The Golden Gate.
The Golden Gate follows a group of young upstarts in this city. The City Lights bookstore in this city helped many Beat Generation novelists get their start.

bonuses.leadin: This novel details the Election of 1952 and the abolition of the Zamindari system. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this single-stranded molecule that, like DNA, contains genetic information. The COVID vaccinesproduced by Moderna and Pfizer use this specific molecule to trigger the immune response.
Messenger RNA is synthesized from DNA in this process, which is sped up by RNA polymerase.

RNA and DNA each have four nitrogenous bases, denoted by letters. The bases adenine, cytosine, andguanine, represented by A, C, and G, are found in both RNA and DNA, but the fourth base is different in eachmolecule. Name either fourth base.

bonuses.leadin: This specific molecule serves as a template to be read by a ribosome to synthesize a protein. For tenpoints each,

parts.text: Name this former Governor of Georgia and 39th President of the United States. He was defeated by Ronald Reagan in the 1980 Presidential Election.
During his presidency, Jimmy Carter engaged in several of these talks with Leonid Brezhnev to derail the development of nuclear arms. Similar talks earlier took place between Nixon and Brezhnev.
With Omar Torrijos, Carter signed two treaties that ceased U.S. control of this structure, which had been constructed in 1914 during the presidency of Teddy Roosevelt.

bonuses.leadin: Pro-segregationist governor Lester Maddox was elected separately as Lieutenant Governor when this man was elected Governor. For ten points each:

parts.text: Name this body whose large mass and retrograde orbit mean it was likely captured from the Kuiper ("kai-per") Belt. Voyager 2 recorded a Bond albedo of 0.89 in the visual region for this body.
Triton is a moon of this planet. The Great (emphasize) Dark Spot is no longer visible on this ice giant.

This phenomenon is a possible cause of Triton's plumes, and it is known to be the source of Enceladus's water-rich plumes. This phenomenon releases low viscosity lava composed of water, dissolved gasses, and salts.

bonuses.leadin: Voyager 2 discovered this body's plumes Mahilani and Hili, which are hypothesized to be driven by a solid-state greenhouse effect. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this nine-day Jewish observance that takes place in November or December, sometimes called the Festival of Lights.
During Hanukkah, celebrants typically light this object, a candelabrum with nine branches.
A common dish eaten during Hanukkah is the latke, a pancake made out of this food.

bonuses.leadin: This holiday celebrates the success of the revolt of the Maccabees against Antiochus IV, and children traditionally play with a dreidel during this celebration. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Jacobean playwright, who wrote about the corruption of Italian society in The White Devil.
Webster's other famous tragedy is named for the Duchess of this place. She is eventually murdered on the orders of her brother Ferdinand.
Webster also collaborated on the comedies Westward Ho and Northward Ho. The comedy Eastward Ho was partially written by this other playwright, who also wrote Volpone.

bonuses.leadin: This author's last solo play was The Devil's Law Case. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this English author of And Then There Were None, whose novel The Mysterious Affair at Styles introduced the character of Hercule Poirot [ayr-KYOOL pwah-ROH].
In this frequently-adapted novel, Hercule Poirot discovers who killed a man travelling under the name "Samuel Ratchett" on a train traveling from Istanbul to Calais.
acceptableAnswers: The Murder on the Orient Express

parts.text: Before solving crimes in England, Poirot was a policeman in Brussels, the capital of this European country.

bonuses.leadin: This author's many book series follow Miss Jane Marple of St Mary Mead, Tommy and Tuppence Beresford, and a round-headed crime-solver with an enormous moustache. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this technique invented by Mikhail Tsvet, in which the mobile phase separates into components as it passes through a stationary phase.

Livengood cites a debate between Tsvet and Leon Marchlewski to argue that chromatography was initially unpopular because it didn't employ this then-ubiquitous process, whose products are separated from the mother liquor.
Tsvet developed chromatography to extract this biomolecule whose porphyrin ("POR-fur-in") ring contains a central magnesium atom.

bonuses.leadin: Historian John Livengood argued against the prevailing wisdom that Richard Willstätter prevented the widespread adoption of this technique until the 1930s. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this ethnic group that faced discrimination when they came in large numbers during the California Gold Rush. This ethnic group was banned from migrating to the United States by a namesake exclusion act.
These 1943 riots in Los Angeles targeted Mexican-Americans and their "pachuco" gangs after the Sleepy Lagoon murder case.

Eleven Italian-Americans were lynched in this city in 1894 for the killing of police officer David Hennessy. This city was also home of the "Axeman" serial killer, whose victims were primarily Italian-Americans.

bonuses.leadin: 26 members of this ethnic group were killed in the Rock Springs Massacre. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country, where long-time dictator Robert Mugabe died in 2019.
A short-lived republic that became Zimbabwe was named after this founder of De Beers Diamond Company, who was prime minister of the Cape Colony in the 1890s.
The builders of Great Zimbabwe were ancestors of this present-day Bantu people, who formed the Kingdom of Mutapa (moo-TAP-uh) under Nyatsimba (nee-AHT-sim-bah).

bonuses.leadin: A "Great" city that shares its name with this country was home to the Eastern Enclosure, where six soapstone sculptures were found. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this period in which the South was drawn into five districts for military occupation by the North.
These people came from the North to the South during Reconstruction seeking profit or political office. Their pejorative name derives from the sacks they supposedly carried their luggage in.
Reconstruction was "ended" in this year. This year also saw a large railroad strike start in Martinsburg, West Virginia.

bonuses.leadin: Its namesake acts required the former Confederate States to ratify the 14th Amendment before being readmitted to the Union. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this functional group, which is simply a carbon atom double bonded to oxygen. Aldehydes posses this functional group at a terminal position.

During this reduction function, a ketone or aldehyde molecule is completely reduced to form an alkane. This reaction involves creating the reactant's hydrazone and then treating it with a strong base.
The Tollens's test, which is used to distinguish between aldehydes and ketones, makes use of this metal's nitrate. This metal has atomic number 47 chemical symbol Ag.

bonuses.leadin: Two of these functional groups are separated by an oxygen atom in acid anhydride molecules, and molecules with this functional group are reduced in the Clemmsensen reaction. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this home country of the author of "Poems for Moscow," Marina Tsvetaeva, as well as the poet who created a 2014 translation of Tsvataeva's works, Ilya Kaminsky.
Kaminsky also translated this Soviet poet's collection Northern Elegies. This author declared that "one hundred million voices shout" through her "tortured mouth" in her poem Requiem.

Akhmatova's Poem Without [one of these people] was dedicated to the "fellow citizens who perished in Leningrad." The literary theory of the "monomyth" is also known as the journey of one of these people.

bonuses.leadin: One poet from this country described the "Spassky Gates...and the Chapel of Stars." For ten points each:

parts.text: In one scene, this character is rolled up in a carpet and thrown in the air after another character refuses to pay for a night in an inn. This faithful squire rides the donkey Dapple and helps in his master's search for Dulcinea.
Sancho Panza accompanies this knight of a Miguel Cervantes novel who mistakes a host of windmills for giants.
In Don Quixote, a duke and duchess offer to make Sancho the governor of a village they call an "island" of this name.

bonuses.leadin: A parable by Kafka reveals the "truth" about this character. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with stomach anatomy.
What is the main function of the esophagus in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to stomach anatomy.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name these maritime vessels operated by companies such as Cunard and White Star. Unlike cruise ships, boats of this type existed primarily to transport passengers across large bodies of water on a fixed schedule, and they have since largely been rendered obsolete.
Perhaps the most famous ocean liner is this one, a British liner that sank in the northern Atlantic Ocean after colliding with an iceberg on her 1912 maiden voyage to New York City.

Ocean liners were often requisitioned for military purposes, either as transport or prison ships. Two of these German liners, one named for a region on the island of Rugen ("ROO-gun"), the other named for a Swiss Nazi leader, both sunk in the Baltic Sea in 1945, and remain two of the largest maritime losses of life in history. Name either.

bonuses.leadin: Apart from his innovations in railway engineering, Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed three early examples of these vessels, each of which became the largest by gross tonnage at the time of their building. For 10 points each:

parts.text: A farewell by Wang Wei is one of many Chinese poems to reference "white" examples of what objects, and claims they persist for all time?
This Chinese poet, whose "Farewell Song of the White Clouds" describes clouds floating over Chu, also wrote about gazing at the moon in "Quiet Night Thought".
In this author's story "The Poetry Cloud," Li Bai meets a god named Li Bai who builds a computer to write poetry. This Chinese sci-fi author wrote The Three-Body Problem.

bonuses.leadin: Han Shan wrote a poem about men who "ask their way through" these objects and a poem whose speaker resides among 1,000 of these objects and 10,000 streams. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this sociological theory that posits that people form beliefs based on their individual environment and engagement with other people. Supported by George Herbert Mead, this theory emphasizes qualitative research like participant observation.

The theory of symbolic interactionism can be used to explain an individual's place in society based on these concepts which vary depending on the social situation. Examples of these concepts include parent, teacher, or artist.

A very important role concerns this concept that might influence familial or cultural attitudes. The social construction of this concept was developed by Judith Butler in her book on this concept's Trouble.

bonuses.leadin: The founder of this theory, Herbert Blumer, said that "Most human and humanizing activity that people engage in is talking to each other." For 10 points each:
